question: How is that comprehensive view of cognition presented here?
premises: Some hold that in certain cases cognition is full with a complete grasp of both sequence and nonsequence.
The text introduces this as their view.
Here that view is presented only by a brief indication.
inference: The doctrine of cognition encompassing both sequence and nonsequence is acknowledged but only sketched in this passage.
plain_english: In some cases they consider it to be full with a complete grasp of both sequence and nonsequence; for now that view is shown only by a brief indication.
